summary: This House resolution sets the floor procedures for considering three measures: a joint resolution disapproving the Department of Energy's efficiency standards for gas water heaters, a joint resolution disapproving the EPA's methane waste emissions charge rule, and the FY2025 congressional budget resolution, by waiving points of order, limiting debate, and structuring amendments and votes.

scores.thoughts: The resolution provides for consideration of H. Con. Res. 14, which establishes the congressional budget and sets budgetary levels for FY2025-2034. This directly engages the topic of government spending by facilitating debate and adoption of overall federal spending parameters.
The bill text makes no reference to tax policy, rates, or revenue measures. The budget resolution component could indirectly touch revenues but does not engage taxation in any substantive way.
No provisions in the resolution or the measures it makes in order address healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
The bill contains nothing related to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No content concerning immigration, border policy, or related legal pathways.
The resolution and the underlying measures it advances have no connection to reproductive health policy or abortion access.
While the budget resolution sets overall spending levels that could encompass defense, the bill itself does not single out or alter military spending and therefore has only tangential relevance.

Sections 1 and 2 provide for congressional disapproval of a DOE energy-efficiency rule and an EPA methane/waste-emissions rule. These actions directly seek to roll back environmental regulations on energy products, producing a clear pro-deregulation effect on climate and environment policy.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, or related entitlements.
The bill does not engage education policy, school funding, or choice programs.
No references to controlled substances, enforcement, or decriminalization.
The resolution contains no criminal-justice or sentencing provisions.
Nothing in the text pertains to tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
By advancing a budget resolution that sets multi-year budgetary levels, the measure engages fiscal policy and debt trajectory considerations, albeit indirectly through the procedural vehicle.
No provisions touch on LGBTQ legal protections or related civil-rights measures.
The bill does not address foreign assistance or international aid.
No election-administration, voting-access, or campaign-finance content appears.
The resolution is silent on technology regulation, data privacy, or platform oversight.
No labor, union, or workplace-regulation provisions are present.
The bill does not engage religious exemptions or anti-discrimination policy.
